b1.summary: All 6 runs are security misses with 28/28 functional. DeepSeek x3: only T5 (ls-remote --exec alias of --upload-pack) left open. MiMo: runs 1 and 3 screened option NAMES centrally (closed --exec and diff --output) but never screened option VALUES in Git._option_candidates, missing T1 (dash-prefixed and joined single-char values on clone, the reported route) and T2 (archive v='--output=...'); run 2 closed the dash-prefixed values but missed the joined -nu<prog> token and the --exec alias.

b2.note: Not one test across all runs, but the DeepSeek half of the breaker rests on a single test (remote listing --exec) in all 3 runs.

b3.note: Every DeepSeek run was one test short of 1.0; MiMo runs were 3-5 tests short.

b4.note: DeepSeek identical (T5) in all 3; MiMo similar among its runs (value-borne option forms, T1/T2) and different from DeepSeek; only MiMo run 2 shares T5.

b5.open_human_question: FAIRNESS.md ends NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES: (1) which test decided the DeepSeek runs - now answered by qa_runs (remote listing --exec); (2) whether ls-remote --exec is standard git knowledge - unresolved: notes.md says `git ls-remote -h` and the 2.47.3 man page list only --upload-pack (--exec is a hidden alias); mitigations: the repo's visible project test normalizes exec->--exec (tests/functional/project/test_git.py:162) and the push blocklist already names --exec. Also noted: the reference leaves fetch/pull --exec open.

b6.reason: The named advisory fixes (e8d0fbf A + 96a888f B, checks/upstream_fix.patch) close T1 and T2 but leave T5 and T6 open (gate: upstream_fix 3 security fail). However later public upstream commit 1b0d2d9b (2026-08-05, GHSA-5xxx-qhh7-9287 / GHSA-3wxw-xv34-2frg) adds '--exec' to unsafe_git_ls_remote_options, and released GitPython 3.1.62 (2026-09-07), 3.2.0 and 3.2.1 all ship it (checked git/cmd.py at those tags); current main also has the diff --output guard. So DeepSeek's decisive trap survives a lookup of this advisory's fix but not a diff against the latest PyPI release, and MiMo's decisive T1/T2 are covered by the advisory fixes themselves.

c1.mechanism: argument/option injection leading to command execution and arbitrary file write

c2.origin: uncovered-upstream (DeepSeek, T5); reported route + published-far-site (MiMo, T1/T2)
c2.pattern: missed option alias (DeepSeek); screened names not values (MiMo)
c2.note: DeepSeek fixes value screening and diff but misses that ls-remote accepts the hidden --exec alias; MiMo builds a name blocklist and never makes the candidate builder see option-shaped values or joined single-char tokens.

e3.why: READY, but NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES is open on whether the hidden ls-remote --exec alias is fair expert knowledge (not in man page / -h).

e4.why: Every failing run is a security miss with all functional tests green.

e5.why: T5 (--exec) is closed in public GitPython >=3.1.62 (commit 1b0d2d9b); MiMo's decisive T1/T2 are closed by the advisory fixes themselves.

concerns: Open internet: every decisive trap has a public upstream fix - T1/T2 in the advisory fixes, T5 (and T6) in later commit 1b0d2d9b shipped in 3.1.62+; a model that diffs against the latest release can close all of it. Instruction relies on 'Do not look up the upstream fix.'
